title: Surjectivity of affine-limit points detects local finite presentation for schemes
statement: Let $B$ and $U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $g:U\to B$ be a morphism, and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose that for every small nonempty directed set $I$ and every inverse system of affine $B$-schemes $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ with limit $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the canonical map of sets $$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Mor}_B(T_i,U)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mor}_B(T,U)$$ is surjective. Here the colimit is a filtered colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $g$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No injectivity of the comparison map, quasi-compactness, or quasi-separatedness of $B$ or $U$ is assumed.

proof.text: Fix affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq U$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$ with $g(W)\subseteq V$. For an arbitrary small nonempty directed system of $R$-algebras $A_i$, put $A=\operatorname{colim}_i A_i$. Given an $R$-map $h:C\to A$, the spectrum correspondence gives a $V$-map $a:T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$. The spectrum-colimit lemma identifies $T$ with the limit of $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and makes all transitions affine. Compose their $V$-structures with $V\hookrightarrow B$ to obtain an affine $B$-test system.

source.place: Tag 0CM0 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), first two paragraphs: affine charts and the directed algebra system

proof.text: Apply the assumed surjectivity to the composite $T\xrightarrow{a}W\hookrightarrow U$. Every element of a filtered colimit of sets has a stage representative, so there are $i$ and a $B$-map $b_i:T_i\to U$ with $b_i\circ p_i=(W\hookrightarrow U)\circ a$, where $p_i:T\to T_i$ is the limit projection.

source.place: Tag 0CM0 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), third paragraph: descend the composite map into the whole scheme

proof.text: Let $O_i=b_i^{-1}(W)\subseteq T_i$. The equality in Step 2 gives $p_i^{-1}(O_i)=T$. Each $T_k$ is quasi-compact because it is affine; Step 1 supplies affine transitions. Apply the eventual-open-containment lemma to this limit cone and $O_i$: there is $j\geq i$ such that $t_{ji}^{-1}(O_i)=T_j$. Thus $b_i\circ t_{ji}$ has image in $W$. The lemma requires no quasi-compactness of $O_i$.

source.place: Tag 0CM0 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), last paragraph: closed-complement compactness argument, via its existing eventual-open-containment consequence

proof.text: Restrict the continuous map and structure-sheaf map of $b_i\circ t_{ji}$ to the open subscheme $W$. This gives $a_j:T_j\to W$ with $(W\hookrightarrow U)\circ a_j=b_i\circ t_{ji}$. Both $T_j\to V$ obtained from this equality agree after $V\hookrightarrow B$, hence agree: an open-subscheme inclusion is injective on maps, by restriction of the same space and sheaf maps. Thus $a_j$ is a $V$-map. Likewise its pullback to $T$ equals $a$, since these maps agree after $W\hookrightarrow U$. By the spectrum correspondence the $R$-map $h_j:C\to A_j$ associated to $a_j$ therefore satisfies $(A_j\to A)\circ h_j=h$.

source.place: Tag 0CM0 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), middle and last paragraphs: restrict into the open and recover the algebra homomorphism

proof.text: Steps 1--4 factor every $R$-map $C\to\operatorname{colim}_i A_i$ through some $A_j$. Apply the directed-Hom algebra criterion (Tag 00QO) to conclude that $C$ is finitely presented over $R$. For any $u\in U$, choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $g(u)$ and then an affine neighbourhood $W$ of $u$ inside $g^{-1}(V)$, using the affine-open basis of a scheme. The finite presentation just proved witnesses finite presentation at $u$. The definition therefore makes $g$ locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0CM0 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), first paragraph and conclusion: Algebra Tag 00QO and the affine-local definition
